rules.statement: Don't report a style preference the codebase itself doesn't follow; report only issues you can point to at a specific line in the code.
rules.why: The review prompt limits findings to concrete, locatable problems and excludes style preferences foreign to the codebase.
rules.check: Before raising a style finding, check whether sibling code in the repository follows that style; if it doesn't, or the finding can't be tied to a file and line, drop it.

rules.statement: Don't add new code that duplicates a helper, extension or pattern the codebase already provides; reuse the existing one.
rules.why: The review checks fit with existing patterns and flags anything duplicated that already exists.
rules.check: For each new helper or utility in the diff, search the repository for an existing equivalent and flag the duplicate.

rules.statement: A change to a public API or to the shape of stored data must stay backward compatible, or come with a migration and an explicit note of the break.
rules.why: The review treats backward compatibility of public APIs and stored data, and migrations, as risks to check.
rules.check: Look for removed or renamed public members, changed signatures, and changed persisted fields or schemas without a migration or a documented breaking change.
